newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan feed body says to discuss mould on U.S. corn.
newsitem.headline: Japan feed body says to discuss mould on U.S. corn.

text.p: The Japan Feed Trade Association said on Monday it would discuss a mould problem with U.S. corn at a committee meeting on October 31.
Local traders said some U.S. corn cargoes that arrived at Japanese ports recently had been found to have mould because of higher-than-usual moisture content.
"We'll raise the mould problem at a committee meeting this Thursday. Chances are we may officially request the U.S. side to solve it as soon as possible," an association official said.
Japan is a major buyer of corn, which is used for making feed here. It imported 11.59 million tonnes from the United States in calendar 1995.
Japanese traders said the mould was probably caused by the failure of some U.S. exporters to dry the crop sufficiently at the time of shipment.
When global grain supplies showed extreme tightness earlier this year, U.S. traders were forced to ship a new crop, which usually holds moisture, they said.
